# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

# Operation Specifications
Board::clone
Summary: Produces a deep copy of the board so that agents and the game can safely mutate their own copy.
Algorithm:
  copy = new Board(size)
  for each tile (x,y):
      create a new Tile with the same x and y
      copy tile colour from tiles[x][y]
      set visited = false in the copy
      assign the new Tile to copy.tiles[x][y]
  copy.winner = winner
  return copy
Related Features: size, tiles, winner
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: None.
Output: A new Board object with the same size, same tile colours, and same winner.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: The returned board is independent of the original; further changes to one do not affect the other. Traversal marks in the clone are cleared.

Board::equals
Summary: Compares two boards for logical equality based on board size and tile colours.
Algorithm:
  if o == this:
      return true
  if o == null or o is not a Board:
      return false
  other = (Board) o
  if size != other.size:
      return false
  for each coordinate (x,y):
      if tiles[x][y].colour != other.tiles[x][y].colour:
          return false
  return true
Related Features: size, tiles, Tile.colour
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour
Input: o: the object to compare against.
Output: true if the other object is a Board with the same size and the same tile colours.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: The board's state is unchanged. Traversal marks and cached winner are not considered part of equality.

Board::clearTiles
Summary: Clears all traversal/visited marks on every tile of the board.
Algorithm:
  for x from 0 to size-1:
      for y from 0 to size-1:
          tiles[x][y].clearVisit()
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Tile
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: Every tile has visited == false. Tile colours and winner are unchanged.

Board::hasEnded
Summary: Determines whether the given colour has a winning connected path across the board, and caches the winner if found.
Algorithm:
  if colour == null or colour == Colour.EMPTY:
      return false
  if winner == colour:
      return true
  if winner != Colour.EMPTY:
      return false
  clearTiles()
  if colour == Colour.RED:
      for y from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[0][y].colour == RED:
              dfsColour(0, y, RED)
      for y from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[size-1][y].visited:
              winner = RED
              return true
  if colour == Colour.BLUE:
      for x from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[x][0].colour == BLUE:
              dfsColour(x, 0, BLUE)
      for x from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[x][size-1].visited:
              winner = BLUE
              return true
  return false
Related Features: size, tiles, winner, clearTiles, dfsColour, Tile.colour, Tile.visited
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: colour: the colour to test for a winning path.
Output: true if the given colour has won; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: If the colour has won, winner is set to that colour and true is returned. Otherwise, winner remains unchanged and false is returned.

Board::dfsColour
Summary: Performs a depth-first traversal over same-coloured tiles starting from a specified coordinate, marking visited tiles.
Algorithm:
  if x or y is outside [0, size-1]:
      return
  if colour == Colour.EMPTY:
      return
  tile = tiles[x][y]
  if tile.visited or tile.colour != colour:
      return
  tile.visit()
  for k from 0 to Tile.NEIGHBOUR_COUNT-1:
      dfsColour(x + Tile.iDisplacements[k], y + Tile.jDisplacements[k], colour)
Related Features: size, tiles, Tile.visited, Tile.colour, Tile.x, Tile.y, Tile.visit, Tile.NEIGHBOUR_COUNT, Tile.iDisplacements, Tile.jDisplacements
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x and y are board coordinates; colour is the stone colour to trace.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized. If x,y are outside bounds, the method returns without effect.
Post-condition: All not-already-visited tiles of the given colour reachable from (x,y) through Hex neighbours are marked visited.

Board::setTileColour
Summary: Sets the colour of the tile at the given coordinate.
Algorithm:
  if x or y is outside [0, size-1]:
      throw IllegalArgumentException
  if colour == null:
      throw IllegalArgumentException
  tiles[x][y].colour = colour
Related Features: size, tiles, Tile.colour
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x and y are board coordinates; colour is the new tile colour.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: x and y must be valid board coordinates; colour must be non-null.
Post-condition: The specified tile's colour is updated. Traversal marks and cached winner are not changed.

Related Features: size, tiles, Tile.visited, Tile.colour, Tile.visit, Tile.NEIGHBOUR_COUNT, Tile.iDisplacements, Tile.jDisplacements
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x and y are board coordinates; colour is the stone colour to trace.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized. If x,y are outside bounds, the method returns without effect.
Post-condition: All not-already-visited tiles of the given colour reachable from (x,y) through Hex neighbours are marked visited.

      throw IllegalArgumentException
  if colour == null:

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

# Operation Specifications
Board::clone
Summary: Produces a deep copy of the board so that agents and the game can safely mutate their own copy.
Algorithm:
  copy = new Board(size)
  for each tile (x,y):
      create a new Tile with the same x and y
      copy tile colour from tiles[x][y]
      copy visited state from tiles[x][y]
      assign the new Tile to copy.tiles[x][y]
  copy.winner = winner
  return copy
Related Features: size, tiles, winner, Tile.colour, Tile.visited
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour
Input: None.
Output: A new Board object with the same size, same tile colours, same visited marks, and same winner.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: The returned board is independent of the original; further changes to one do not affect the other. Traversal marks and winner are the same as in the original at the time of cloning.

Board::equals
Summary: Compares two boards for logical equality based on board size and tile colours.
Algorithm:
  if o == this:
      return true
  if o == null or o is not a Board:
      return false
  other = (Board) o
  if size != other.size:
      return false
  for each coordinate (x,y):
      if tiles[x][y].colour != other.tiles[x][y].colour:
          return false
  return true
Related Features: size, tiles, Tile.colour
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour
Input: o: the object to compare against.
Output: true if the other object is a Board with the same size and the same tile colours.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: The board's state is unchanged. Traversal marks and cached winner are not considered part of equality.

Board::clearTiles
Summary: Clears all traversal/visited marks on every tile of the board.
Algorithm:
  for x from 0 to size-1:
      for y from 0 to size-1:
          tiles[x][y].clearVisit()
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Tile
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: Every tile has visited == false. Tile colours and winner are unchanged.

Board::hasEnded
Summary: Determines whether the given colour has a winning connected path across the board, and caches the winner if found.
Algorithm:
  if colour == null or colour == Colour.EMPTY:
      return false
  if winner == colour:
      return true
  if winner != Colour.EMPTY:
      return false
  clearTiles()
  if colour == Colour.RED:
      for y from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[0][y].colour == RED:
              dfsColour(0, y, RED)
      for y from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[size-1][y].visited:
              winner = RED
              return true
  if colour == Colour.BLUE:
      for x from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[x][0].colour == BLUE:
              dfsColour(x, 0, BLUE)
      for x from 0 to size-1:
          if tiles[x][size-1].visited:
              winner = BLUE
              return true
  return false
Related Features: size, tiles, winner, clearTiles, dfsColour, Tile.colour, Tile.visited
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: colour: the colour to test for a winning path.
Output: true if the given colour has won; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: If the colour has won, winner is set to that colour and true is returned. Otherwise, winner remains unchanged and false is returned.

Board::dfsColour
Summary: Performs a depth-first traversal over same-coloured tiles starting from a specified coordinate, marking visited tiles.
Algorithm:
  if x or y is outside [0, size-1]:
      return
  if colour == Colour.EMPTY:
      return
  tile = tiles[x][y]
  if tile.visited or tile.colour != colour:
      return
  tile.visit()
  for k from 0 to Tile.NEIGHBOUR_COUNT-1:
      dfsColour(x + Tile.iDisplacements[k], y + Tile.jDisplacements[k], colour)
Related Features: size, tiles, Tile.visited, Tile.colour, Tile.visit, Tile.NEIGHBOUR_COUNT, Tile.iDisplacements, Tile.jDisplacements
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x and y are board coordinates; colour is the stone colour to trace.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized. If x,y are outside bounds, the method returns without effect.
Post-condition: All not-already-visited tiles of the given colour reachable from (x,y) through Hex neighbours are marked visited.

Board::setTileColour
Summary: Sets the colour of the tile at the given coordinate and invalidates any cached winner.
Algorithm:
  if x or y is outside [0, size-1]:
      throw IllegalArgumentException
  if colour == null:
      throw IllegalArgumentException
  tiles[x][y].colour = colour
  winner = Colour.EMPTY
Related Features: size, tiles, winner, Tile.colour
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x and y are board coordinates; colour is the new tile colour.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: x and y must be valid board coordinates; colour must be non-null.
Post-condition: The specified tile's colour is updated. Any previously cached winner is reset to Colour.EMPTY. Traversal marks are unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Game::endGame
Summary: Builds the final result map for a finished game using the termination status.
Algorithm:
  now = System.nanoTime()
  totalTime = nsToS(now - startTime)
  winMethod = status.name()
  if status == EndState.WIN:
      winner = players.get(board.winner).name if board.winner != Colour.EMPTY else ""
  else if status == EndState.TIMEOUT or status == EndState.BAD_MOVE:
      winner = players.get(currentPlayer.oppColour()).name
  else: // FAILED_LOAD
      winner = ""
  return formatResult(
      player1.name, player2.name, winner, winMethod,
      nsToS(player1.moveTime), nsToS(player2.moveTime),
      player1.turn, player2.turn,
      player1.turn + player2.turn,
      totalTime)
Related Features: board, players, player1, player2, currentPlayer, startTime, formatResult, nsToS
Related Classes: Player, Board, Colour, EndState, EMap
Input: status: EndState.WIN, TIMEOUT, BAD_MOVE, or FAILED_LOAD.
Output: An EMap containing keys: player1, player2, winner, win_method, player1_move_time, player2_move_time, player1_turns, player2_turns, total_turns, total_game_time. Time values are in seconds with millisecond precision.
Pre-condition: The game has been initialized and startTime is set.
Post-condition: The game state is unchanged; the result map representing the final outcome is returned.

Game::run
Summary: Top-level entry point for a game. It starts the clock, delegates to play(), and converts an unexpected runtime failure into a FAILED_LOAD result.
Algorithm:
  if startTime == 0:
      startTime = System.nanoTime()
  try:
      return play()
  catch RuntimeException ex:
      if logWriter != null:
          logWriter.println(ex)
      return endGame(EndState.FAILED_LOAD)
Related Features: startTime, play, endGame, logWriter, logIsStderr
Related Classes: EndState, EMap
Input: None.
Output: The final game result EMap.
Pre-condition: The Game should already be initialized with players, board, and logging configuration.
Post-condition: The game has been played, or a failure has been recorded, and a result map is returned.

Game::makeMove
Summary: Applies an already validated move to the game state, including normal stone placement, the second-turn swap option, turn count advancement, and current-player alternation.
Algorithm:
  if m.x == -1 and m.y == -1:
      // swap move
      hasSwapped = true
      exchange the colour-to-player associations in players for RED and BLUE
      // currentPlayer stays the same colour; that colour now belongs to the opponent,
      // so the original first player has the next turn.
  else:
      board.setTileColour(m.x, m.y, currentPlayer)
      currentPlayer = currentPlayer.oppColour()
  turn = turn + 1
Related Features: board, currentPlayer, hasSwapped, turn, players
Related Classes: Move, Board, Colour, Player
Input: m: the legal Move to apply.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: m has been accepted by isValidMove. The game is initialized and not already finished.
Post-condition: For a normal move, the selected tile is occupied by the current player's colour. For a swap move, only the player-colour associations are exchanged. The turn counter is incremented, and the next side to move is set appropriately.

Game::isValidMove
Summary: Checks whether a proposed move is legal in the current game state.
Algorithm:
  if move == null:
      return false
  if board.winner != Colour.EMPTY:
      return false
  if move.x == -1 and move.y == -1:
      return turn == 2 and hasSwapped == false
  if move.x < 0 or move.x >= board.size:
      return false
  if move.y < 0 or move.y >= board.size:
      return false
  return board.tiles[move.x][move.y].colour == Colour.EMPTY
Related Features: turn, hasSwapped
Related Classes: Move, Board, Tile, Colour
Input: move: the proposed Move; turn: the current 1-based move number; board: the current Board.
Output: true if the move is legal; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: board is non-null and turn is the move number about to be played.
Post-condition: No game state is changed.

Game::play
Summary: Runs the core game loop: asks the current agent for a move, validates it, applies it, checks win/timeout/invalid-move termination, and updates player timing/turn statistics.
Algorithm:
  if startTime == 0:
      startTime = System.nanoTime()
  oppMove = null
  while true:
      side = currentPlayer
      player = players.get(side)
      start = System.nanoTime()
      move = player.agent.makeMove(turn, board, oppMove)
      elapsed = System.nanoTime() - start
      player.moveTime = player.moveTime + elapsed
      if player.moveTime > maximumTime:
          return endGame(EndState.TIMEOUT)
      if not isValidMove(move, turn, board):
          return endGame(EndState.BAD_MOVE)
      player.turn = player.turn + 1
      makeMove(move)
      if board.hasEnded(side):
          return endGame(EndState.WIN)
      oppMove = move
Related Features: startTime, currentPlayer, players, board, turn, maximumTime, isValidMove, makeMove, endGame
Related Classes: Move, Board, Player, AgentBase, Colour, EndState, EMap
Input: None.
Output: The final result EMap produced by endGame.
Pre-condition: The Game has been initialized through init; player1 and player2 are set up under the correct initial colours.
Post-condition: The game is played to termination by WIN, TIMEOUT, or BAD_MOVE, and the corresponding result map is returned.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::endGame
Summary: Builds the final result map for a finished game using the termination status.
Algorithm:
  now = System.nanoTime()
  totalTime = nsToS(now - startTime)
  winMethod = status.name()
  if status == EndState.WIN:
      winner = players.get(board.winner).name if board.winner != Colour.EMPTY else ""
  else if status == EndState.TIMEOUT or status == EndState.BAD_MOVE:
      winner = players.get(currentPlayer.oppColour()).name
  else: // FAILED_LOAD
      winner = ""
  return formatResult(
      player1.name, player2.name, winner, winMethod,
      nsToS(player1.moveTime), nsToS(player2.moveTime),
      player1.turn, player2.turn,
      player1.turn + player2.turn,
      totalTime)
Related Features: board, players, player1, player2, currentPlayer, startTime, formatResult, nsToS
Related Classes: Player, Board, Colour, EndState, EMap
Input: status: EndState.WIN, TIMEOUT, BAD_MOVE, or FAILED_LOAD.
Output: An EMap containing keys: player1, player2, winner, win_method, player1_move_time, player2_move_time, player1_turns, player2_turns, total_turns, total_game_time. Time values are in seconds with millisecond precision.
Pre-condition: The game has been initialized and startTime is set.
Post-condition: The game state is unchanged; the result map representing the final outcome is returned.

Game::run
Summary: Top-level entry point for a game. It starts the clock, delegates to play(), and converts an unexpected runtime failure into a FAILED_LOAD result.
Algorithm:
  if startTime == 0:
      startTime = System.nanoTime()
  try:
      return play()
  catch RuntimeException ex:
      if logWriter != null:
          logWriter.println(ex)
      return endGame(EndState.FAILED_LOAD)
Related Features: startTime, play, endGame, logWriter, logIsStderr
Related Classes: EndState, EMap
Input: None.
Output: The final game result EMap.
Pre-condition: The Game should already be initialized with players, board, and logging configuration.
Post-condition: The game has been played, or a failure has been recorded, and a result map is returned.

Game::makeMove
Summary: Applies an already validated move to the game state, including normal stone placement, the second-turn swap option, turn count advancement, and current-player alternation.
Algorithm:
  if m.x == -1 and m.y == -1:
      // swap move
      hasSwapped = true
      exchange the colour-to-player associations in players for RED and BLUE
      // currentPlayer stays the same colour; that colour now belongs to the opponent,
      // so the original first player has the next turn.
  else:
      board.setTileColour(m.x, m.y, currentPlayer)
      currentPlayer = currentPlayer.oppColour()
  turn = turn + 1
Related Features: board, currentPlayer, hasSwapped, turn, players
Related Classes: Move, Board, Colour, Player
Input: m: the legal Move to apply.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: m has been accepted by isValidMove. The game is initialized and not already finished.
Post-condition: For a normal move, the selected tile is occupied by the current player's colour. For a swap move, only the player-colour associations are exchanged. The turn counter is incremented, and the next side to move is set appropriately.

Game::isValidMove
Summary: Checks whether a proposed move is legal in the current game state.
Algorithm:
  if move == null:
      return false
  if board.winner != Colour.EMPTY:
      return false
  if move.x == -1 and move.y == -1:
      return turn == 2 and hasSwapped == false
  if move.x < 0 or move.x >= board.size:
      return false
  if move.y < 0 or move.y >= board.size:
      return false
  return board.tiles[move.x][move.y].colour == Colour.EMPTY
Related Features: turn, hasSwapped
Related Classes: Move, Board, Tile, Colour
Input: move: the proposed Move; turn: the current 1-based move number; board: the current Board.
Output: true if the move is legal; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: board is non-null and turn is the move number about to be played.
Post-condition: No game state is changed.

Game::play
Summary: Runs the core game loop: asks the current agent for a move, validates it, applies it, checks win/timeout/invalid-move termination, and updates player timing/turn statistics.
Algorithm:

      startTime = System.nanoTime()
  oppMove = null
  while true:
      side = currentPlayer
      player = players.get(side)
      start = System.nanoTime()

      elapsed = System.nanoTime() - start

      player.turn = player.turn + 1
      makeMove(move)
      if board.hasEnded(side):
          return endGame(EndState.WIN)
      oppMove = move
Related Features: startTime, currentPlayer, players, board, turn, maximumTime, isValidMove, makeMove, endGame
Related Classes: Move, Board, Player, AgentBase, Colour, EndState, EMap
Input: None.
Output: The final result EMap produced by endGame.

      throw IllegalArgumentException
  if colour == Colour.RED:
      return Colour.BLUE
  else:
      return Colour.RED

Post-condition: The agent's state is unchanged.

Algorithm:

      return 0
  return colour.hashCode()
Related Features: colour
Related Classes: Colour
Input: None.
Output: An int hash code.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: The agent's state is unchanged. Two agents with the same non-null colour produce the same hash code.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

   * Algorithm:
   *   for x from 0 to size-1:
   *       for y from 0 to size-1:
   *           tiles[x][y].clearVisit()
   * Related Features: size, tiles, Tile.clearVisit
   * Related Classes: Tile
   * Input: None.
   * Output: void.
   * Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
   * Post-condition: Every tile has visited == false. Tile colours and winner are unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void clearTiles()
  {
    for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
    {
      for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
      {
        tiles[x][y].clearVisit();
      }
    }
  }

  public String printBoard()
  {
    StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
    {
      for (int space = 0; space < y; space++)
      {
        result.append(' ');
      }
      for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
      {
        Colour c = tiles[x][y].getColour();
        result.append(c == Colour.RED ? 'R' : c == Colour.BLUE ? 'B' : '.');
        if (x < size - 1)
        {
          result.append(' ');
        }
      }
      result.append('\n');
    }
    return result.toString();
  }

  public Board clone()

    Tile[][] copyTiles = new Tile[size][size];

    {

        newTile.setVisited(source.isVisited());
        newTile.setIDisplacements(source.getIDisplacements().clone());
        newTile.setJDisplacements(source.getJDisplacements().clone());
        copyTiles[x][y] = newTile;
      }
    }
    copy.setTiles(copyTiles);
    copy.setWinner(getWinner());
    return copy;
  }

   * Algorithm:

   * Post-condition: The game is played to termination by WIN, TIMEOUT, or BAD_MOVE, and the corresponding result map is returned.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, String> play()
  {
    if (startTime == 0L)
    {
      startTime = System.nanoTime();
    }
    Move oppMove = null;
    while (true)
    {
      Colour side = getCurrentPlayer();
      Player player = getPlayers().get(side);
      Board boardCopy = getBoard().clone();
      long start = System.nanoTime();
      Move move = player.getAgent().makeMove(getTurn(), boardCopy, oppMove);
      long elapsed = System.nanoTime() - start;
      player.setMoveTime(player.getMoveTime() + elapsed);
      if (player.getMoveTime() > getMaximumTime())
      {
        return endGame(EndState.TIMEOUT);
      }
      if (!isValidMove(move, getTurn(), getBoard()))
      {
        return endGame(EndState.BAD_MOVE);
      }
      player.setTurn(player.getTurn() + 1);
      makeMove(move);
      if (getBoard().hasEnded(getHelper().colourOpposite(getCurrentPlayer())))
      {
        return endGame(EndState.WIN);
      }
      oppMove = move;
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Applies an already validated move to the game state, including normal stone placement, the second-turn swap option, turn count advancement, and side-to-move update.
   * Algorithm:
   *   if m.x == -1 and m.y == -1:
   *       // swap move
   *       hasSwapped = true
   *       swap the colours of player1.agent and player2.agent
   *       update players so that each player is keyed by its agent's colour
   *       // currentPlayer stays the same colour; that colour now belongs to the opponent,
   *       // so the original first player has the next turn.
   *   else:
   *       board.setTileColour(m.x, m.y, currentPlayer)
   *       currentPlayer = helper.colourOpposite(currentPlayer)
   *   turn = turn + 1
   * Related Features: board, currentPlayer, hasSwapped, turn, players, player1, player2, helper
   * Related Classes: Move, Board, Colour, Player, AgentBase, HexHelper
   * Input: m: the legal Move to apply.
   * Output: void.
   * Pre-condition: m has been accepted by isValidMove. The game is initialized and not already finished.
   * Post-condition: For a normal move, the selected tile is occupied by the colour that made the move. For a swap move, the players' agent colours and the players map are exchanged. The turn counter is incremented, and the next side to move is set appropriately.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void makeMove(final Move m)
  {
    if (m.getX() == -1 && m.getY() == -1)
    {
      setHasSwapped(true);
      Colour player1Colour = getPlayer1().getAgent().getColour();
      Colour player2Colour = getPlayer2().getAgent().getColour();
      getPlayer1().getAgent().setColour(player2Colour);
      getPlayer2().getAgent().setColour(player1Colour);
      getPlayers().clear();
      getPlayers().put(getPlayer1().getAgent().getColour(), getPlayer1());
      getPlayers().put(getPlayer2().getAgent().getColour(), getPlayer2());
    }
    else
    {
      getBoard().setTileColour(m.getX(), m.getY(), getCurrentPlayer());
      setCurrentPlayer(getHelper().colourOpposite(getCurrentPlayer()));
    }
    setTurn(getTurn() + 1);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Builds the final result map for a finished game using the termination status.
   * Algorithm:
   *   now = System.nanoTime()
   *   totalTime = nsToS(now - startTime)
   *   winMethod = status.name()
   *   if status == EndState.WIN:
   *       winner = players.get(board.winner).name if board.winner != Colour.EMPTY else ""
   *   else if status == EndState.TIMEOUT or status == EndState.BAD_MOVE:
   *       winner = players.get(helper.colourOpposite(currentPlayer)).name
   *   else: // FAILED_LOAD
   *       winner = ""
   *   return formatResult(
   *       player1.name, player2.name, winner, winMethod,
   *       nsToS(player1.moveTime), nsToS(player2.moveTime),
   *       player1.turn, player2.turn,
   *       player1.turn + player2.turn,
   *       totalTime)
   * Related Features: board, players, player1, player2, currentPlayer, startTime, helper, formatResult, nsToS
   * Related Classes: Player, Board, Colour, EndState, HexHelper, EMap
   * Input: status: EndState.WIN, TIMEOUT, BAD_MOVE, or FAILED_LOAD.
   * Output: An EMap containing keys: player1, player2, winner, win_method, player1_move_time, player2_move_time, player1_turns, player2_turns, total_turns, total_game_time. Time values are in seconds with millisecond precision.
   * Pre-condition: The game has been initialized, startTime is set, and helper is available.
   * Post-condition: The game state is unchanged; the result map representing the final outcome is returned.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, String> endGame(final EndState status)
  {
    long now = System.nanoTime();
    double totalTime = nsToS(now - startTime);
    String winMethod = status.name();
    String winner;
    if (status == EndState.WIN)
    {
      winner = (getBoard().getWinner() != Colour.EMPTY) ? getPlayers().get(getBoard().getWinner()).getName() : "";
    }
    else if (status == EndState.TIMEOUT || status == EndState.BAD_MOVE)
    {
      winner = getPlayers().get(getHelper().colourOpposite(getCurrentPlayer())).getName();
    }
    else // FAILED_LOAD
    {
      winner = "";
    }
    return formatResult(
        getPlayer1().getName(), getPlayer2().getName(), winner, winMethod,
        nsToS(getPlayer1().getMoveTime()), nsToS(getPlayer2().getMoveTime()),
        getPlayer1().getTurn(), getPlayer2().getTurn(),
        getPlayer1().getTurn() + getPlayer2().getTurn(),
        totalTime);
  }

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

@startuml

title hexgame Model

abstract class AgentBase {
    colour : Colour
    hashCode() : int
    makeMove(turn : int, board : Board, oppMove : Move) : Move

}

    size : int
    tiles : tilearray
    winner : Colour
    clearTiles() : void

    equals(o : EJavaObject) : boolean
    hasEnded(colour : Colour) : boolean

}

    currentPlayer : Colour
    hasSwapped : boolean

    logWriter : PrintWriter
    maximumTime : long
    players : EMap
    startTime : long

    board : Board
    helper : HexHelper

    player2 : Player

    init(player1 : Player, player2 : Player, boardSize : int, logWriter : PrintWriter, logIsStderr : boolean) : void
    isValidMove(move : Move, turn : int, board : Board) : boolean
    makeMove(m : Move) : void
    nsToS(t : long) : double
    play() : EMap
    run() : EMap
}
class HexHelper {
    boardFromString(stringInput : String, boardSize : int) : Board
    colourFromChar(c : char) : Colour
    colourGetChar(colour : Colour) : String
    colourOpposite(colour : Colour) : Colour
    createBoard(boardSize : int) : Board
}
class Move {
    x : int
    y : int
    toString() : String
}
class Player {
    moveTime : long
    name : String
    turn : int
    agent : AgentBase
}
class Tile {
    NEIGHBOUR_COUNT : int
    colour : Colour
    iDisplacements : IntArrary
    jDisplacements : IntArrary
    visited : boolean
    x : int
    y : int
    clearVisit() : void
    visit() : void
}
enum Colour {
    EMPTY
    RED
    BLUE
}
enum EndState {
    WIN
    TIMEOUT
    BAD_MOVE
    FAILED_LOAD
}

Game *-- Board : board
Game --> HexHelper : helper
Game --> Player : player1
Game --> Player : player2
Player --> AgentBase : agent
@enduml

6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;

8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. # Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

# Operation Specifications
Board::setTileColour
Summary: Sets the colour of the tile at a specified coordinate.
Algorithm: Locate the tile at (x, y) and assign its colour field to the given colour.
  Reset the cached winner to EMPTY because the board contents have changed.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x, y - row and column coordinates in [0, size-1]; colour - the Colour to assign, including EMPTY.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: x and y are valid coordinates; colour is non-null.
Post-condition: The tile at (x, y) has the requested colour; cached winner is reset to EMPTY.

Board::equals
Summary: Compares this board with another object for equality.
Algorithm: If the other object is the same object, return true. If it is not a Board,
  return false. Compare board size and then compare the colour at every board coordinate.
  Visited flags and the cached winner are ignored because they are derived/transient state.
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour, EJavaObject
Input: o - the object to compare to.
Output: boolean true if the other object is a Board with the same dimensions and same tile colours.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: No side effects.

Board::clearTiles
Summary: Clears the traversal marks on every tile.
Algorithm: Iterate over all tiles in `tiles` and call `clearVisit()` on each tile.
Related Features: tiles
Related Classes: Tile
Input: None.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized and its tiles array is non-null.
Post-condition: Every tile has visited == false. Tile colours, coordinates, and the cached winner remain unchanged.

Board::hasEnded
Summary: Determines whether the given colour has a winning connected path.
Algorithm:
  - If colour is null or EMPTY, return false.
  - Set cached winner to EMPTY and clear all visited flags.
  - If colour == RED: start DFS from every tile on the top edge (row 0) that is RED.
    Then check whether any tile on the bottom edge (row size-1) is RED and visited.
    If so, set winner to RED, clear visited flags, and return true.
  - If colour == BLUE: start DFS from every tile on the left edge (column 0) that is BLUE.
    Then check whether any tile on the right edge (column size-1) is BLUE and visited.
    If so, set winner to BLUE, clear visited flags, and return true.
  - Clear visited flags and return false.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner, clearTiles, dfsColour
Related Classes: Colour, Tile
Input: colour - RED or BLUE.
Output: boolean true if that colour has a connecting path between its two target edges.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized; colour is RED or BLUE.
Post-condition: If a winning path exists, winner is set to the winning colour; otherwise winner is EMPTY.
  All visited flags are cleared.

Board::dfsColour
Summary: Performs a depth-first traversal from a tile and marks all connected
  same-colour tiles as visited.
Algorithm:
  - If x or y is outside [0, size-1], return.
  - Get the tile at (x, y). If the tile is already visited or its colour is not the
    requested colour, return.
  - Mark the tile visited.
  - For k in 0..NEIGHBOUR_COUNT-1, compute nx = x + Tile.iDisplacements[k],
    ny = y + Tile.jDisplacements[k], and recursively call dfsColour(nx, ny, colour).
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x, y - row and column coordinates; colour - the colour to follow, normally RED or BLUE.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized; colour is RED or BLUE. Out-of-range coordinates are ignored.
Post-condition: All same-colour tiles connected to the starting tile through the six Hex
  neighbour directions have visited == true.

Board::clone
Summary: Creates an independent deep copy of this board.
Algorithm: Create a new Board with the same size and cached winner. For each tile,
  create a new Tile with the same x, y, and colour, and with visited == false.
  The new board shares no mutable tile objects with the original.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour
Input: None.
Output: A new Board with the same stone layout and winner.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: The original board is unchanged; the clone has the same size, colours,
  and winner, fresh visited flags, and can be modified independently.

# Operation Specifications
Board::setTileColour
Summary: Sets the colour of the tile at a specified coordinate.
Algorithm: Locate the tile at (x, y) and assign its colour field to the given colour.
  Reset the cached winner to EMPTY because the board contents have changed.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x, y - row and column coordinates in [0, size-1]; colour - the Colour to assign, including EMPTY.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: x and y are valid coordinates; colour is non-null.
Post-condition: The tile at (x, y) has the requested colour; cached winner is reset to EMPTY.

Board::equals
Summary: Compares this board with another object for equality.
Algorithm: If the other object is the same object, return true. If it is not a Board,
  return false. Compare board size and then compare the colour at every board coordinate.
  Visited flags and the cached winner are ignored because they are derived/transient state.
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour, EJavaObject
Input: o - the object to compare to.
Output: boolean true if the other object is a Board with the same dimensions and same tile colours.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: No side effects.

Board::clearTiles
Summary: Clears the traversal marks on every tile.
Algorithm: Iterate over all tiles in `tiles` and call `clearVisit()` on each tile.
Related Features: tiles
Related Classes: Tile
Input: None.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized and its tiles array is non-null.
Post-condition: Every tile has visited == false. Tile colours, coordinates, and the cached winner remain unchanged.

Board::hasEnded
Summary: Determines whether the given colour has a winning connected path.
Algorithm:
  - If colour is null or EMPTY, return false.
  - Set cached winner to EMPTY and clear all visited flags.
  - If colour == RED: start DFS from every tile on the top edge (row 0) that is RED.
    Then check whether any tile on the bottom edge (row size-1) is RED and visited.
    If so, set winner to RED, clear visited flags, and return true.
  - If colour == BLUE: start DFS from every tile on the left edge (column 0) that is BLUE.
    Then check whether any tile on the right edge (column size-1) is BLUE and visited.
    If so, set winner to BLUE, clear visited flags, and return true.
  - Clear visited flags and return false.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner, clearTiles, dfsColour
Related Classes: Colour, Tile
Input: colour - RED or BLUE.
Output: boolean true if that colour has a connecting path between its two target edges.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized; colour is RED or BLUE.
Post-condition: If a winning path exists, winner is set to the winning colour; otherwise winner is EMPTY.
  All visited flags are cleared.

Board::dfsColour
Summary: Performs a depth-first traversal from a tile and marks all connected
  same-colour tiles as visited.
Algorithm:
  - If x or y is outside [0, size-1], return.
  - Get the tile at (x, y). If the tile is already visited or its colour is not the
    requested colour, return.
  - Mark the tile visited.
  - For k in 0..NEIGHBOUR_COUNT-1, compute nx = x + Tile.iDisplacements[k],
    ny = y + Tile.jDisplacements[k], and recursively call dfsColour(nx, ny, colour).
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x, y - row and column coordinates; colour - the colour to follow, normally RED or BLUE.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized; colour is RED or BLUE. Out-of-range coordinates are ignored.
Post-condition: All same-colour tiles connected to the starting tile through the six Hex
  neighbour directions have visited == true.

Board::clone
Summary: Creates an independent deep copy of this board.
Algorithm: Create a new Board with the same size and cached winner. For each tile,
  create a new Tile with the same x, y, and colour, and with visited == false.
  The new board shares no mutable tile objects with the original.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour
Input: None.
Output: A new Board with the same stone layout and winner.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: The original board is unchanged; the clone has the same size, colours,
  and winner, fresh visited flags, and can be modified independently.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```
