# Operation Specifications
Board::setTileColour
Summary: Sets the colour of the tile at a specified coordinate.
Algorithm: Locate the tile at (x, y) and assign its colour field to the given colour.
  Reset the cached winner to EMPTY because the board contents have changed.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x, y - row and column coordinates in [0, size-1]; colour - the Colour to assign, including EMPTY.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: x and y are valid coordinates; colour is non-null.
Post-condition: The tile at (x, y) has the requested colour; cached winner is reset to EMPTY.

Board::equals
Summary: Compares this board with another object for equality.
Algorithm: If the other object is the same object, return true. If it is not a Board,
  return false. Compare board size and then compare the colour at every board coordinate.
  Visited flags and the cached winner are ignored because they are derived/transient state.
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour, EJavaObject
Input: o - the object to compare to.
Output: boolean true if the other object is a Board with the same dimensions and same tile colours.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: No side effects.

Board::clearTiles
Summary: Clears the traversal marks on every tile.
Algorithm: Iterate over all tiles in `tiles` and call `clearVisit()` on each tile.
Related Features: tiles
Related Classes: Tile
Input: None.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized and its tiles array is non-null.
Post-condition: Every tile has visited == false. Tile colours, coordinates, and the cached winner remain unchanged.

Board::hasEnded
Summary: Determines whether the given colour has a winning connected path.
Algorithm:
  - Clear all visited flags.
  - If colour is null or EMPTY, return false.
  - If colour == RED:
      Start DFS from every tile on the top edge (row 0) that is RED.
      If any tile on the bottom edge (row size-1) is RED and visited,
      set winner to RED, clear visited flags, and return true.
  - If colour == BLUE:
      Start DFS from every tile on the left edge (column 0) that is BLUE.
      If any tile on the right edge (column size-1) is BLUE and visited,
      set winner to BLUE, clear visited flags, and return true.
  - Clear visited flags and return false.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner, clearTiles, dfsColour
Related Classes: Colour, Tile
Input: colour - the colour to check; RED and BLUE are the playing colours. EMPTY/null returns false.
Output: boolean true if colour has a connecting path between its two target edges; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: All visited flags are cleared. If colour is RED or BLUE and has a winning path,
  winner is set to that colour; otherwise the cached winner remains unchanged.

Board::dfsColour
Summary: Performs a depth-first traversal from a tile and marks all connected
  same-colour tiles as visited, provided the starting tile is valid, unvisited,
  and of the requested colour; otherwise it does nothing.
Algorithm:
  - If x or y is outside [0, size-1], return.
  - Let tile be the tile at (x, y).
  - If tile is already visited or its colour is not the requested colour, return.
  - Mark tile visited (for example, tile.visit()).
  - For k in 0..NEIGHBOUR_COUNT-1, compute
      nx = x + tile.iDisplacements[k],
      ny = y + tile.jDisplacements[k],
    and recursively call dfsColour(nx, ny, colour).
Related Features: size, tiles
Related Classes: Tile, Colour
Input: x, y - row and column coordinates; out-of-range coordinates are ignored.
  colour - the colour to follow, normally RED or BLUE.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized; colour is RED or BLUE.
Post-condition: If the tile at (x, y) is within bounds, unvisited, and has the requested
  colour, then every tile reachable from it through connected same-colour tiles via the
  six Hex neighbour directions has visited == true. Otherwise no tile is newly visited.

Board::clone
Summary: Creates an independent deep copy of this board.
Algorithm: Create a new Board with the same size and cached winner. For each tile,
  create a new Tile with the same x, y, and colour, and with visited == false.
  The new board shares no mutable tile objects with the original.
Related Features: size, tiles, winner
Related Classes: Board, Tile, Colour
Input: None.
Output: A new Board with the same stone layout and winner.
Pre-condition: The board is initialized.
Post-condition: The original board is unchanged; the clone has the same size, colours,
  and winner, fresh visited flags, and can be modified independently.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::isValidMove
Summary: Validates a proposed move.
Algorithm:
  - If move or board is null, return false.
  - If move is the special swap move (-1, -1), return true only if turn == 2 and the swap has not already been used.
  - Otherwise, return true only if x and y are within [0, board.size-1] and the target tile is EMPTY.
Related Features: hasSwapped
Related Classes: Move, Board, Colour
Input: move - the Move to validate; turn - the current 1-based move number; board - the board on which to validate.
Output: boolean true if the move is legal, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: None; invalid inputs are handled by returning false.
Post-condition: No side effects.

Game::run
Summary: Public entry point for running a game and returning the result map.
Algorithm:
  - If the game is not initialized (for example, no board or no players), return endGame(FAILED_LOAD).
  - If startTime is not already set, set it to the current time.
  - Call play() and return its result.
  - If an unexpected exception is thrown before or during play, return endGame(FAILED_LOAD).
Related Features: board, player1, player2, startTime, play, endGame
Related Classes: Board, Player, EndState, EMap
Input: None.
Output: EMap final game result.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Either the game is played and its result is returned, or a result map with FAILED_LOAD is returned.

Game::endGame
Summary: Builds the final game-result map after a game has ended.
Algorithm:
  - Determine the winner name and win method:
    * WIN: winner is the player mapped from board.winner; win_method = "WIN".
    * TIMEOUT: currentPlayer is the player who timed out; winner is the other player; win_method = "TIMEOUT".
    * BAD_MOVE: currentPlayer is the player who made the invalid move; winner is the other player; win_method = "BAD_MOVE".
    * FAILED_LOAD: winner = "none"; win_method = "FAILED_LOAD".
  - Convert player move times and total game time from nanoseconds to seconds with
    millisecond precision using nsToS.
  - Call formatResult with player names, winner, win method, move times, turn counts,
    total turns, and total game time.
Related Features: currentPlayer, player1, player2, players, board, startTime, turn, formatResult, nsToS
Related Classes: EndState, Player, Board, Colour, EMap
Input: status - one of WIN, TIMEOUT, BAD_MOVE, or FAILED_LOAD.
Output: EMap containing keys: player1, player2, winner, win_method, player1_move_time,
  player2_move_time, player1_turns, player2_turns, total_turns, total_game_time.
Pre-condition: The game is initialized. If status is WIN, board.winner must be non-EMPTY.
Post-condition: No board state is mutated; a result map is returned.

Game::play
Summary: Runs the main game loop and returns the final result map.
Algorithm:
  1. Ensure startTime is set.
  2. lastMove = null.
  3. Loop until a result is returned:
     - mover = players.get(currentPlayer); if null, return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
     - boardCopy = board.clone().
     - moveStart = now; try move = mover.agent.makeMove(turn, boardCopy, lastMove); catch any exception and return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
     - mover.moveTime += now - moveStart.
     - If mover.moveTime > maximumTime, return endGame(TIMEOUT).
     - If !isValidMove(move, turn, board), return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
     - movedColour = currentPlayer.
     - Call makeMove(move).
     - lastMove = move.
     - If move is not a swap and board.hasEnded(movedColour), return endGame(WIN).
Related Features: currentPlayer, turn, players, player1, player2, board, maximumTime, startTime, hasSwapped, isValidMove, makeMove, endGame
Related Classes: AgentBase, Player, Board, Move, Colour, EndState, EMap
Input: None.
Output: EMap final game result.
Pre-condition: The game has been initialized with two players, a board, and maximumTime; currentPlayer is RED and turn is 1-based.
Post-condition: The game is over; no further moves are made; the result map is returned.

Game::makeMove
Summary: Applies a legal move to the game state.
Algorithm:
  - This method may be called only after isValidMove has returned true.
  - Record the current mover as players.get(currentPlayer).
  - If the move is (-1, -1):
      * Set hasSwapped = true.
      * Exchange the colours assigned to player1 and player2, and update the players lookup so each colour points to the new owner.
      * Leave currentPlayer as the same colour, because the other participant now owns that colour and is next to move.
  - Otherwise:
      * Place the current player's colour on the board with board.setTileColour(m.x, m.y, currentPlayer).
      * Set currentPlayer to the opposite colour.
  - Increment mover.turn and Game.turn.
Related Features: currentPlayer, hasSwapped, players, player1, player2, board, turn
Related Classes: Move, Board, Player, Colour
Input: m - the legal Move to apply; (-1, -1) denotes a swap move.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The game is initialized; m is legal according to isValidMove.
Post-condition: For a normal move, the stone is placed and the current player alternates.
  For a swap, hasSwapped is true and the players exchange colours. Turn counts are advanced.

    * FAILED_LOAD: winner = "none"; win_method = "FAILED_LOAD".
  - Convert player move times and total game time from nanoseconds to seconds with
    millisecond precision using nsToS.
  - Call formatResult with player names, winner, win method, move times, turn counts,
    total turns, and total game time.
Related Features: currentPlayer, player1, player2, players, board, startTime, turn, formatResult, nsToS
Related Classes: EndState, Player, Board, Colour, EMap
Input: status - one of WIN, TIMEOUT, BAD_MOVE, or FAILED_LOAD.
Output: EMap containing keys: player1, player2, winner, win_method, player1_move_time,
  player2_move_time, player1_turns, player2_turns, total_turns, total_game_time.
Pre-condition: The game is initialized. If status is WIN, board.winner must be non-EMPTY.
Post-condition: No board state is mutated; a result map is returned.

Game::play
Summary: Runs the main game loop and returns the final result map.
Algorithm:
  1. Ensure startTime is set.
  2. lastMove = null.
  3. Loop until a result is returned:
     - mover = players.get(currentPlayer); if null, return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
     - boardCopy = board.clone().
     - moveStart = now; try move = mover.agent.makeMove(turn, boardCopy, lastMove); catch any exception and return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
     - mover.moveTime += now - moveStart.
     - If mover.moveTime > maximumTime, return endGame(TIMEOUT).
     - If !isValidMove(move, turn, board), return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
     - movedColour = currentPlayer.
     - Call makeMove(move).
     - lastMove = move.
     - If move is not a swap and board.hasEnded(movedColour), return endGame(WIN).
Related Features: currentPlayer, turn, players, player1, player2, board, maximumTime, startTime, hasSwapped, isValidMove, makeMove, endGame
Related Classes: AgentBase, Player, Board, Move, Colour, EndState, EMap
Input: None.
Output: EMap final game result.
Pre-condition: The game has been initialized with two players, a board, and maximumTime; currentPlayer is RED and turn is 1-based.
Post-condition: The game is over; no further moves are made; the result map is returned.

Game::makeMove
Summary: Applies a legal move to the game state.
Algorithm:
  - This method may be called only after isValidMove has returned true.
  - Record the current mover as players.get(currentPlayer).
  - If the move is (-1, -1):
      * Set hasSwapped = true.
      * Exchange the colours assigned to player1 and player2, and update the players lookup so each colour points to the new owner.
      * Leave currentPlayer as the same colour, because the other participant now owns that colour and is next to move.
  - Otherwise:
      * Place the current player's colour on the board with board.setTileColour(m.x, m.y, currentPlayer).
      * Set currentPlayer to the opposite colour.
  - Increment mover.turn and Game.turn.
Related Features: currentPlayer, hasSwapped, players, player1, player2, board, turn
Related Classes: Move, Board, Player, Colour
Input: m - the legal Move to apply; (-1, -1) denotes a swap move.
Output: None.
Pre-condition: The game is initialized; m is legal according to isValidMove.
Post-condition: For a normal move, the stone is placed and the current player alternates.
  For a swap, hasSwapped is true and the players exchange colours. Turn counts are advanced.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall / Domain Description

This system models the board game Hex. Two players, RED and BLUE, take turns placing stones on a hexagonal grid represented as a square two-dimensional array. RED wins by forming a connected path from the top edge of the board to the bottom edge. BLUE wins by forming a connected path from the left edge to the right edge.

The implementation should focus on the core game model: board state, tiles, moves, players, agents, turn execution, win detection, and game result reporting. The board uses hex-style adjacency, so each tile has up to six neighbours rather than four. Empty cells are represented by Colour.EMPTY, separately from RED and BLUE stones.

The code should follow the class structure given in the UML. Constructors and ordinary accessors may be implemented as needed for object initialization and testing, but the main behavior should be driven by the model classes and their business responsibilities.

## 2. Functional Requirement

`Colour` represents cell/player colour states: EMPTY, RED, and BLUE. RED and BLUE are the two player sides; EMPTY represents an unoccupied board cell or no winner.

`Move` represents a position selected by an agent. A normal move stores board coordinates. The special coordinate pair `(-1, -1)` represents a swap move. Its string representation must be `"SWAP()"`; ordinary moves must be formatted as `"(x=<x>, y=<y>)"`.

`Tile` represents one board cell. It stores its coordinate, current colour, visited state, and the six neighbour displacement directions used by the Hex grid. A tile can be marked visited and later cleared. The six neighbour offsets should correspond to the standard slanted Hex board layout.

`Board` owns the board size, all tiles, and the winner if one has been found. It should support placing a colour at a coordinate, printing the board, cloning board state, clearing traversal marks, and detecting whether a colour has won. Win detection should search through connected same-colour tiles using the six Hex-neighbour directions. RED starts from the top edge and tries to reach the bottom edge; BLUE starts from the left edge and tries to reach the right edge. Board printing should use `"R"` for RED, `"B"` for BLUE, and `"0"` for empty cells, with cells separated by spaces and rows separated by newlines.

`AgentBase` is the base abstraction for game agents. Each agent has a colour and must provide a move when given the current turn, a board copy, and the opponent's previous move. It should also be able to determine the opposite colour. An invalid or missing colour should be treated as an error when asking for the opposite colour.

`Player` stores the participant name, the associated agent, accumulated move time, and number of turns taken.

`Game` coordinates a match between two players. It initializes the board, starts RED as the first player, alternates turns, asks the current agent for a move, validates moves, applies legal moves, handles the swap move on the second turn, checks for wins, tracks each player's elapsed move time, and ends the game when a player wins, times out, or makes an invalid move. The per-player time limit is five minutes expressed in nanoseconds. Time values reported to users should be converted from nanoseconds to seconds with millisecond precision.

The game result should be returned as a map of strings that includes the player names, winner, win method, per-player move times, per-player turn counts, total turns, and total game time. The keys expected by clients are `player1`, `player2`, `winner`, `win_method`, `player1_move_time`, `player2_move_time`, `player1_turns`, `player2_turns`, `total_turns`, and `total_game_time`.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`HexHelper` is an external helper class and should not be generated from the main UML. It provides colour conversion using `"R"`, `"B"`, and `"0"`, opposite-colour lookup, fully initialized board creation, and board loading from newline-separated, space-separated text.
```

   * Algorithm:

   *   1. Ensure startTime is set.
   *   2. lastMove = null.
   *   3. Loop until a result is returned:

   *      - movedColour = currentPlayer.
   *      - Call makeMove(move).
   *      - lastMove = move.
   *      - If move is not a swap and board.hasEnded(movedColour), return endGame(WIN).

1. Compute context information
  1.1 Consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.2 Locate these files in your project.
  1.3 Generate the class summarization.
2. A method is unimplemented if its body contains `// TODO: Please complete this Java method based on the docstring`.
3. For every unimplemented method, 
  3.1 You must read the docstring of this method. The fragment between `<!-- begin-model-doc -->` and `<!-- end-model-doc -->` contains the method specification;
  3.2 Generate your code strictly according to the algorithm; Be aware of the EMF code style and APIs;
  3.3 You should not change the method signature;
  3.4 After generation, replace the current body with the one you generate;
  3.5 Keep and update the docstring by changing `@generated` to `@generated NOT`.
4. Check the import list. Add missing imports if needed.
5. Do not change other part.
6. Be aware of the method signatures, particularly, the input and output types, provided in the context.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Public entry point for running a game and returning the result map.
   * Algorithm:
   *   - If the game is not initialized (for example, no board or no players), return endGame(FAILED_LOAD).
   *   - If startTime is not already set, set it to the current time.
   *   - Call play() and return its result.
   *   - If an unexpected exception is thrown before or during play, return endGame(FAILED_LOAD).
   * Related Features: board, player1, player2, startTime, play, endGame
   * Related Classes: Board, Player, EndState, EMap
   * Input: None.
   * Output: EMap final game result.
   * Pre-condition: None.
   * Post-condition: Either the game is played and its result is returned, or a result map with FAILED_LOAD is returned.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, String> run()
  {
    try
    {
      if (getBoard() == null || getPlayer1() == null || getPlayer2() == null)
      {
        return endGame(EndState.FAILED_LOAD);
      }
      if (getStartTime() == 0)
      {
        setStartTime(System.nanoTime());
      }
      return play();
    }
    catch (Exception e)
    {
      return endGame(EndState.FAILED_LOAD);
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Validates a proposed move.
   * Algorithm:
   *   - If move or board is null, return false.
   *   - If move is the special swap move (-1, -1), return true only if turn == 2 and the swap has not already been used.
   *   - Otherwise, return true only if move.x and move.y are within [0, board.size-1] and the tile at that coordinate has colour Colour.EMPTY.
   * Related Features: hasSwapped
   * Related Classes: Move, Board, Tile, Colour
   * Input: move - the Move to validate; turn - the current 1-based move number; board - the board on which to validate.
   * Output: boolean true if the move is legal, false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: None; invalid inputs are handled by returning false.
   * Post-condition: No side effects.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model required="true" turnRequired="true" boardRequired="true"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isValidMove(final Move move, final int turn, final Board board)
  {
    if (move == null || board == null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    if (move.getX() == -1 && move.getY() == -1)
    {
      return turn == 2 && !isHasSwapped();
    }
    return move.getX() >= 0 && move.getX() < board.getSize()
        && move.getY() >= 0 && move.getY() < board.getSize()
        && board.getTiles()[move.getX()][move.getY()].getColour() == Colour.EMPTY;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @generated
   */
  public void init(final Player player1, final Player player2, final int boardSize, final PrintWriter logWriter, final boolean logIsStderr)
  {
    setPlayer1(player1);
    setPlayer2(player2);
    setLogWriter(logWriter);
    setLogIsStderr(logIsStderr);
    setHelper(HexgameFactory.eINSTANCE.createHexHelper());
    setBoard(getHelper().createBoard(boardSize));
    Map<Colour, Player> newPlayers = new HashMap<Colour, Player>();
    newPlayers.put(Colour.RED, player1);
    newPlayers.put(Colour.BLUE, player2);
    setPlayers(newPlayers);
    setCurrentPlayer(Colour.RED);
    setTurn(1);
    setHasSwapped(false);
    setStartTime(0);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Runs the main game loop and returns the final result map.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Ensure startTime is set.
   *   2. lastMove = null.
   *   3. Loop until a result is returned:
   *      - mover = players.get(currentPlayer); if null, return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
   *      - boardCopy = board.clone().
   *      - moveStart = now; try move = mover.agent.makeMove(turn, boardCopy, lastMove); catch any exception and return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
   *      - mover.moveTime += now - moveStart.
   *      - If mover.moveTime > maximumTime, return endGame(TIMEOUT).
   *      - If !isValidMove(move, turn, board), return endGame(BAD_MOVE).
   *      - movedColour = currentPlayer.
   *      - Call makeMove(move).
   *      - lastMove = move.
   *      - If move is not a swap and board.hasEnded(movedColour), return endGame(WIN).
   * Related Features: currentPlayer, turn, players, player1, player2, board, maximumTime, startTime, hasSwapped, isValidMove, makeMove, endGame
   * Related Classes: AgentBase, Player, Board, Move, Colour, EndState, EMap
   * Input: None.
   * Output: EMap final game result.
   * Pre-condition: The game has been initialized with two players, a board, and maximumTime; currentPlayer is RED and turn is 1-based.
   * Post-condition: The game is over; no further moves are made; the result map is returned.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, String> play()
  {
    if (getStartTime() == 0)
    {
      setStartTime(System.nanoTime());
    }
    Move lastMove = null;
    while (true)
    {
      Player mover = getPlayers().get(getCurrentPlayer());
      if (mover == null)
      {
        return endGame(EndState.BAD_MOVE);
      }
      Board boardCopy = getBoard().clone();
      long moveStart = System.nanoTime();
      Move move;
      try
      {
        move = mover.getAgent().makeMove(getTurn(), boardCopy, lastMove);
      }
      catch (Exception e)
      {
        return endGame(EndState.BAD_MOVE);
      }
      mover.setMoveTime(mover.getMoveTime() + (System.nanoTime() - moveStart));
      if (mover.getMoveTime() > getMaximumTime())
      {
        return endGame(EndState.TIMEOUT);
      }
      if (!isValidMove(move, getTurn(), getBoard()))
      {
        return endGame(EndState.BAD_MOVE);
      }
      Colour movedColour = getCurrentPlayer();
      makeMove(move);
      lastMove = move;
      if (!(move.getX() == -1 && move.getY() == -1) && getBoard().hasEnded(movedColour))
      {
        return endGame(EndState.WIN);
      }
    }
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Applies a legal move to the game state.
   * Algorithm:
   *   - This method may be called only after isValidMove has returned true.
   *   - Record the current mover as players.get(currentPlayer).
   *   - If the move is (-1, -1):
   *       * Set hasSwapped = true.
   *       * Exchange the colours assigned to player1 and player2, and update the players lookup so each colour points to its new owner.
   *       * Leave currentPlayer unchanged, because the other participant now owns that colour and is next to move.
   *   - Otherwise:
   *       * Place the current player's colour on the board with board.setTileColour(move.x, move.y, currentPlayer).
   *       * Set currentPlayer = helper.colourOpposite(currentPlayer).
   *   - Increment mover.turn and Game.turn.
   * Related Features: currentPlayer, hasSwapped, players, player1, player2, board, turn, helper
   * Related Classes: Move, Board, Player, Colour, HexHelper
   * Input: m - the legal Move to apply; (-1, -1) denotes a swap move.
   * Output: None.
   * Pre-condition: The game is initialized; m is legal according to isValidMove.
   * Post-condition: For a normal move, the stone is placed and currentPlayer is set to the opposite colour. For a swap, hasSwapped is true and the players exchange colours. Turn counts are advanced.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void makeMove(final Move m)
  {
    Player mover = getPlayers().get(getCurrentPlayer());
    if (m.getX() == -1 && m.getY() == -1)
    {
      setHasSwapped(true);
      Colour player1Colour = null;
      Colour player2Colour = null;
      for (Map.Entry<Colour, Player> entry : getPlayers().entrySet())
      {
        if (entry.getValue() == getPlayer1())
        {
          player1Colour = entry.getKey();
        }
        else if (entry.getValue() == getPlayer2())
        {
          player2Colour = entry.getKey();
        }
      }
      getPlayers().put(player1Colour, getPlayer2());
      getPlayers().put(player2Colour, getPlayer1());
    }
    else
    {
      getBoard().setTileColour(m.getX(), m.getY(), getCurrentPlayer());
      setCurrentPlayer(getHelper().colourOpposite(getCurrentPlayer()));
    }
    mover.setTurn(mover.getTurn() + 1);
    setTurn(getTurn() + 1);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Builds the final game-result map after a game has ended.
   * Algorithm:
   *   - Determine the winner name and win method:
   *     * WIN: winnerName = players.get(board.winner).name; winMethod = "WIN".
   *     * TIMEOUT: winnerName = players.get(helper.colourOpposite(currentPlayer)).name; winMethod = "TIMEOUT".
   *     * BAD_MOVE: winnerName = players.get(helper.colourOpposite(currentPlayer)).name; winMethod = "BAD_MOVE".
   *     * FAILED_LOAD: winnerName = "none"; winMethod = "FAILED_LOAD".
   *   - For FAILED_LOAD, if player1 or player2 is missing, use "none" for its name, 0 for its move time, and 0 for its turn count.
   *   - player1Name = player1 == null ? "none" : player1.name.
   *   - player2Name = player2 == null ? "none" : player2.name.
   *   - player1MoveTime = player1 == null ? 0 : nsToS(player1.moveTime).
   *   - player2MoveTime = player2 == null ? 0 : nsToS(player2.moveTime).
   *   - player1Turn = player1 == null ? 0 : player1.turn.
   *   - player2Turn = player2 == null ? 0 : player2.turn.
   *   - totalTurns = player1Turn + player2Turn.
   *   - totalTime = startTime == 0 ? 0 : nsToS(System.nanoTime() - startTime).
   *   - Call formatResult(player1Name, player2Name, winnerName, winMethod, player1MoveTime, player2MoveTime, player1Turn, player2Turn, totalTurns, totalTime).
   * Related Features: currentPlayer, player1, player2, players, board, startTime, helper, formatResult, nsToS
   * Related Classes: EndState, Player, Board, Colour, HexHelper, EMap
   * Input: status - one of WIN, TIMEOUT, BAD_MOVE, or FAILED_LOAD.
   * Output: EMap containing keys: player1, player2, winner, win_method, player1_move_time, player2_move_time, player1_turns, player2_turns, total_turns, total_game_time.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - For WIN, TIMEOUT, and BAD_MOVE, the game must be initialized and the required players must be present.
   *   - If status is WIN, board.winner must be non-EMPTY.
   *   - FAILED_LOAD may be requested even if initialization failed.
   * Post-condition: No board state is mutated; a result map is returned.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Map<String, String> endGame(final EndState status)
  {
    String winnerName;
    String winMethod;
    switch (status)
    {
      case WIN:
        winnerName = getPlayers().get(getBoard().getWinner()).getName();
        winMethod = "WIN";
        break;
      case TIMEOUT:
        winnerName = getPlayers().get(getHelper().colourOpposite(getCurrentPlayer())).getName();
        winMethod = "TIMEOUT";
        break;
      case BAD_MOVE:
        winnerName = getPlayers().get(getHelper().colourOpposite(getCurrentPlayer())).getName();
        winMethod = "BAD_MOVE";
        break;
      default:
        winnerName = "none";
        winMethod = "FAILED_LOAD";
        break;
    }
    String player1Name = getPlayer1() == null ? "none" : getPlayer1().getName();
    String player2Name = getPlayer2() == null ? "none" : getPlayer2().getName();
    double player1MoveTime = getPlayer1() == null ? 0 : nsToS(getPlayer1().getMoveTime());
    double player2MoveTime = getPlayer2() == null ? 0 : nsToS(getPlayer2().getMoveTime());
    int player1Turn = getPlayer1() == null ? 0 : getPlayer1().getTurn();
    int player2Turn = getPlayer2() == null ? 0 : getPlayer2().getTurn();
    int totalTurns = player1Turn + player2Turn;
    double totalTime = getStartTime() == 0 ? 0 : nsToS(System.nanoTime() - getStartTime());
    return formatResult(player1Name, player2Name, winnerName, winMethod, player1MoveTime, player2MoveTime, player1Turn, player2Turn, totalTurns, totalTime);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @generated
   */
  public Map<String, String> formatResult(final String player1Name, final String player2Name, final String winner, final String winMethod, final double player1MoveTime, final double player2MoveTime, final int player1Turn, final int player2Turn, final double totalTurns, final double totalTime)
  {
    Map<String, String> result = new HashMap<String, String>();
    result.put("player1", player1Name);
    result.put("player2", player2Name);
    result.put("winner", winner);
    result.put("win_method", winMethod);
    result.put("player1_move_time", String.valueOf(player1MoveTime));
    result.put("player2_move_time", String.valueOf(player2MoveTime));
    result.put("player1_turns", String.valueOf(player1Turn));
    result.put("player2_turns", String.valueOf(player2Turn));
    result.put("total_turns", String.valueOf(totalTurns));
    result.put("total_game_time", String.valueOf(totalTime));
    return result;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * @generated
   */
  @Override
  public Object eGet(int featureID, boolean resolve, boolean coreType)
  {
    switch (featureID)
    {
      case HexgamePackage.GAME__MAXIMUM_TIME:
        return getMaximumTime();

  public Map<String, String> run()

  public boolean isValidMove(final Move move, final int turn, final Board board)
  {
    return move != null
        && move.getX() >= 0 && move.getX() < board.getSize()
        && move.getY() >= 0 && move.getY() < board.getSize()
        && board.getTiles()[move.getX()][move.getY()].getColour() == Colour.EMPTY;
  }

  public void init(final Player player1, final Player player2, final int boardSize, final PrintWriter logWriter, final boolean logIsStderr)
  {
     this.turn = 0;
            this.board = helper.createBoard(boardSize);
            this.currentPlayer = Colour.RED;
            this.startTime = System.nanoTime();
            this.hasSwapped = false;
            this.player1 = player1;
            this.player2 = player2;
    
            this.players = new LinkedHashMap<>();
            this.players.put(Colour.RED, this.player1);
            this.players.put(Colour.BLUE, this.player2);
    
            this.logWriter = logWriter;
            this.logIsStderr = logIsStderr;
  }

  public Map<String, String> play()
  {
    Move oppMove = null;
    while (board.getWinner() == Colour.EMPTY)
    {
      Player current = players.get(currentPlayer);
      long moveStart = System.nanoTime();
      Move move = current.getAgent().makeMove(turn, board, oppMove);
      if (!isValidMove(move, turn, board))
      {
        return endGame(EndState.BAD_MOVE);
      }
      makeMove(move);
      oppMove = move;
      current.setTurn(current.getTurn() + 1);
      current.setMoveTime(current.getMoveTime() + (System.nanoTime() - moveStart));
      currentPlayer = currentPlayer == Colour.RED ? Colour.BLUE : Colour.RED;
      turn++;
      if (System.nanoTime() - startTime > maximumTime)
      {
        return endGame(EndState.TIMEOUT);
      }
    }
    return endGame(EndState.WIN);
  }

  public void makeMove(final Move m)
  {
    board.setTileColour(m.getX(), m.getY(), currentPlayer);
  }

  public Map<String, String> endGame(final EndState status)
  {
    Colour winner = board.getWinner();
    String winnerName = winner == Colour.EMPTY ? "" : players.get(winner).getName();
    return formatResult(player1.getName(), player2.getName(), winnerName, status.getLiteral(),
        nsToS(player1.getMoveTime()), nsToS(player2.getMoveTime()),
        player1.getTurn(), player2.getTurn(), turn, nsToS(System.nanoTime() - startTime));
  }
